text: Position of an ant ($\mathrm{S}$ in metres) moving in $\mathrm{Y}$-$\mathrm{Z}$ plane is given by $S=2t^{2}\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ (where $t$ is in second). The magnitude and direction of velocity of the ant at $\mathrm{t}=1\mathrm{s}$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The position of an ant, denoted as $\mathrm{S}$ in meters, moving in the $\mathrm{Y}$-$\mathrm{Z}$ plane is given by $S=2t^{2}\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$, where $t$ is in seconds. To determine the magnitude and direction of the ant's velocity at $t=1$ second, we need to differentiate the position function with respect to time.

The velocity $\vec{\mathrm{v}}$ is given by:

$\vec{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{d\mathrm{S}}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}(2t^{2}\hat{j}+5\hat{k})$

On differentiating, we get:

$\vec{\mathrm{v}}=4t\hat{j}$

At $t=1$ second:

$\vec{\mathrm{v}}=4\cdot 1\hat{j}=4\hat{j}$

Therefore, the magnitude of the velocity is $4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and it is directed along the $y$-axis.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: If the refractive index of the material of a prism is $\cot \left (\frac{A}{2}\right )$, where $A$ is the angle of prism then the angle of minimum deviation will be
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At minimum deviation $δ_{m}$, the refractive index of a prism of angle $A$ is

$μ=\frac{\sin ⎛⎝\dfrac{A+δ_{m}}{2}⎞⎠}{\sin \dfrac{A}{2}}$

With $μ=\cot \dfrac{A}{2}=\dfrac{\cos \frac{A}{2}}{\sin \frac{A}{2}}$:

$\sin \left (\frac{A+δ_{m}}{2}\right )=\cos \frac{A}{2}=\sin \left (\frac{π}{2}-\frac{A}{2}\right )$

Both angles lie between $0$ and $\dfrac{π}{2}$, so

$\frac{A+δ_{m}}{2}=\frac{π}{2}-\frac{A}{2}\Rightarrow δ_{m}=π-2A$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text:
A proton moving with a constant velocity passes through a region of space without any change in its velocity. If $\vec{\mathrm{E}}$ and $\vec{\mathrm{B}}$ represent the electric and magnetic fields respectively, then the region of space may have :

(A) $\mathrm{E}=0,\mathrm{B}=0$

(B) $\mathrm{E}=0,\mathrm{B}\neq 0$

(C) $\mathrm{E}\neq 0,\mathrm{B}=0$

(D) $\mathrm{E}\neq 0,\mathrm{B}\neq 0$

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The velocity stays constant only if the net force on the proton is zero:

$q⃗{E}+q\left (⃗{v}\times ⃗{B}\right )=0$

For $E=0,B=0$, no force acts at all, so this is possible.

For $E=0,B\neq 0$, the magnetic force $q⃗{v}\times ⃗{B}$ vanishes when $⃗{v}$ is parallel or antiparallel to $⃗{B}$, so this is possible.

For $E\neq 0,B=0$, the electric force $q⃗{E}$ acts unbalanced and changes the velocity, so this is not possible.

For $E\neq 0,B\neq 0$, the two forces cancel when $⃗{E}=-⃗{v}\times ⃗{B}$, for example with $⃗{E}$, $⃗{B}$ and $⃗{v}$ mutually perpendicular and $E=vB$ (velocity selector), so this is possible.

The region may therefore have (A), (B) and (D) only.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: A train is moving with a speed of $12\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ on rails which are $1.5\mathrm{m}$ apart. To negotiate a curve of radius $400\mathrm{m}$, the height by which the outer rail should be raised with respect to the inner rail is (Given, $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2})$ :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
On a curve banked so that no sideways force acts on the wheels, $N\cos θ=mg$ and $N\sin θ=\dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}$, so

$\tan θ=\dfrac{v^{2}}{rg}=\dfrac{12^{2}}{400\times 10}=0.036$

The rails are $d=1.5\text{m}$ apart along the inclined track bed, so the outer rail is raised by $h=d\sin θ$. For so small an angle $\sin θ\approx \tan θ$:

$h\approx d\tan θ=1.5\times 0.036=0.054\text{m}=5.4\text{cm}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: Which of the following circuits is reverse - biased?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A p–n junction diode is reverse biased when its n side (the cathode, the bar of the symbol) is connected to a higher potential than its p side (the anode, the triangle).

(A): anode at $+2\text{V}$, cathode connected through R to $-10\text{V}$; the anode is at the higher potential, so the diode is forward biased.

(B): anode at $0\text{V}$ (earth), cathode connected through R to $-5\text{V}$; the anode is at the higher potential, so the diode is forward biased.

(C): anode connected through R to $+2\text{V}$, cathode at $0\text{V}$ (earth); the diode is forward biased.

(D): anode at $+2\text{V}$, cathode connected through R to $+4\text{V}$; the cathode is at the higher potential, so the diode is reverse biased.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: $0.08\mathrm{kg}$ air is heated at constant volume through $5^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. The specific heat of air at constant volume is $0.17\mathrm{kcal}/\mathrm{kg}^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{J}=4.18$ joule/$\mathrm{cal}$. The change in its internal energy is approximately.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the change in the internal energy of air when it is heated at constant volume, we use the formula for heat transfer at constant volume, which is given by:

$\Delta U=mc_{v}\Delta T$

Where:

$\Delta U$ is the change in internal energy,
$m$ is the mass of the substance (in this case, air),
$c_{v}$ is the specific heat at constant volume,
$\Delta T$ is the change in temperature.

Given that:

The mass of air, $m=0.08\text{kg},$
The specific heat of air at constant volume, $c_{v}=0.17\text{kcal/kg}^{\circ }\text{C},$
The change in temperature, $\Delta T=5^{\circ }\text{C},$
And the conversion factor from calories to Joules, $1~\text{cal}=4.18\text{J}.$

First, convert the specific heat from kcal to Joules:

$c_{v}=0.17\text{kcal/kg}^{\circ }\text{C}\times 1000\text{cal/kcal}\times 4.18\text{J/cal}=710.6\text{J/kg}^{\circ }\text{C}$

Now, substitute the values into the formula:

$\Delta U=0.08\times 710.6\times 5$

$\Delta U=284\text{J}$

Thus, the change in internal energy is approximately 284 Joules.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: The radius of third stationary orbit of electron for Bohr's atom is R. The radius of fourth stationary orbit will be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The radius of the nth stationary orbit in the Bohr model of an atom is directly proportional to the square of its principal quantum number n and inversely proportional to the atomic number Z. This relationship is represented by the formula $r_{n}=\frac{n^{2}h^{2}}{4π^{2}kme^{2}Z},$ where :

$n$ is the principal quantum number,

$h$ is Planck's constant,

$k$ is the Coulomb constant,

$m$ is the mass of the electron,

$e$ is the charge of the electron, and

$Z$ is the atomic number of the nucleus (for hydrogen, Z=1).

To find the radius of the fourth orbit ($r_{4}$), in comparison to the third orbit ($r_{3}$), we apply the formula with $n=4$ for the fourth orbit and $n=3$ for the third orbit, and simplify as follows:

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{r_{4}}{r_{3}}=\dfrac{(4^{2})h^{2}}{4π^{2}kme^{2}Z}\div \dfrac{(3^{2})h^{2}}{4π^{2}kme^{2}Z}=\dfrac{(4^{2})}{(3^{2})} \\  \\ =\dfrac{16}{9} \end{array}$

Thus, the radius of the fourth stationary orbit is $\frac{16}{9}$ times the radius of the third stationary orbit, $R$. Therefore, $r_{4}=\frac{16}{9}R$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: A rectangular loop of length $2.5\mathrm{m}$ and width $2\mathrm{m}$ is placed at $60^{\circ }$ to a magnetic field of $4\mathrm{T}$. The loop is removed from the field in $10\sec$. The average emf induced in the loop during this time is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
According to Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction, the induced emf in a closed circuit is equal to the negative rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit. Mathematically, it is expressed as:

$ε=-\frac{d\Phi }{dt}$

Where $ε$ is the induced emf, and $\Phi$ is the magnetic flux.

To find the magnetic flux $\Phi$ through the rectangular loop, we use the formula:

$\Phi =B\cdot A\cdot \cos (θ)$

Where:

$B$ is the magnetic field strength,

$A$ is the area of the loop, and

$θ$ is the angle between the magnetic field lines and the normal (perpendicular) to the plane of the loop.

The area $A$ of the rectangular loop is:

$A=\text{length}\times \text{width}=2.5\mathrm{m}\times 2\mathrm{m}=5\mathrm{m}^{2}$

Given the angle $θ=60^{\circ }$, we can calculate the initial magnetic flux $\Phi _{initial}$:

$\Phi _{initial}=B\cdot A\cdot \cos (60^{\circ })$

$\Phi _{initial}=4\mathrm{T}\cdot 5\mathrm{m}^{2}\cdot \cos (60^{\circ })$

$\Phi _{initial}=4\cdot 5\cdot \frac{1}{2}=10\mathrm{Wb}$

(Since $\cos (60^{\circ })=\frac{1}{2}$)

When the loop is removed from the magnetic field, the final magnetic flux $\Phi _{final}$ is zero, because the loop is no longer within the magnetic field. Thus, the change in magnetic flux $\Delta \Phi$ is:

$\Delta \Phi =\Phi _{final}-\Phi _{initial}=0-10\mathrm{Wb}=-10\mathrm{Wb}$

The loop is removed from the field in $t=10$ seconds, so the rate of change of magnetic flux is:

$\frac{d\Phi }{dt}=\frac{\Delta \Phi }{\Delta t}=\frac{-10\mathrm{Wb}}{10\mathrm{s}}=-1\mathrm{Wb}/\mathrm{s}$

Now we can find the average induced emf $ε$:

$ε=-\frac{d\Phi }{dt}$

$ε=-(-1\mathrm{Wb}/\mathrm{s})$

$ε=+1\mathrm{V}$

Therefore, the average induced emf in the loop during this time is $+1\mathrm{V}$. The correct answer is:

Option C

$+1\mathrm{V}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: A wire of length $10\mathrm{cm}$ and radius $\sqrt{7}\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}$ is connected across the right gap of a meter bridge. When a resistance of $4.5\Omega$ is connected on the left gap by using a resistance box, the balance length is found to be at $60\mathrm{cm}$ from the left end. If the resistivity of the wire is $\mathrm{R}\times 10^{-7}\Omega \mathrm{m}$, then value of $\mathrm{R}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In a balanced meter bridge the ratio of the resistances in the two gaps equals the ratio of the lengths on either side of the balance point. With $4.5\Omega$ in the left gap and the balance point at $60$ cm, the wire in the right gap has resistance $X$:

$\dfrac{4.5}{X}=\dfrac{60}{100-60}=\dfrac{60}{40}\Rightarrow X=3\Omega$

The wire has length $\ell =10\text{cm}=0.1\text{m}$ and radius $r=\sqrt{7}\times 10^{-4}\text{m}$, so its cross-sectional area is

$A=πr^{2}=\dfrac{22}{7}\times 7\times 10^{-8}=22\times 10^{-8}\text{m}^{2}$

Its resistivity is

$ρ=\dfrac{XA}{\ell }=\dfrac{3\times 22\times 10^{-8}}{0.1}=66\times 10^{-7}\Omega \text{m}$

so $R=66$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text:
The average kinetic energy of a monatomic molecule is $0.414\mathrm{eV}$ at temperature :

(Use $K_{B}=1.38\times 10^{-23}\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{mol}-\mathrm{K}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the temperature at which the average kinetic energy of a monatomic molecule is $0.414\text{eV}$, we use the equation for the average kinetic energy of a molecule in terms of temperature:

$K_{\text{avg}}=\frac{3}{2}k_{B}T$

Where:

$K_{\text{avg}}$ is the average kinetic energy
$k_{B}$ is the Boltzmann constant, given as $1.38\times 10^{-23}\text{J/K}$
$T$ is the temperature in Kelvin

First, we need to convert the average kinetic energy from eV to Joules since the Boltzmann constant is in Joules. The conversion factor is $1~\text{eV}=1.6\times 10^{-19}\text{J}$, so:

$K_{\text{avg}}=0.414\text{eV}=0.414\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}\text{J}$

Substituting $K_{\text{avg}}$ and $k_{B}$ into the equation:

$\frac{3}{2}k_{B}T=0.414\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}\text{J}$

Solving for $T$:

$T=\frac{0.414\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}\text{J}}{\frac{3}{2}\times 1.38\times 10^{-23}\text{J/K}}$

After performing the calculations:

$T\approx 3200\text{K}$

Therefore, the temperature at which the average kinetic energy of a monatomic molecule is $0.414\text{eV}$ is approximately 3200 K.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: A particle starts from origin at $t=0$ with a velocity $5\hat{i}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ and moves in $x-y$ plane under action of a force which produces a constant acceleration of $(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j})\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. If the $x$-coordinate of the particle at that instant is $84\mathrm{m}$, then the speed of the particle at this time is $\sqrt{α}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. The value of $α$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The initial velocity $5\hat{i}\text{m s}^{-1}$ has no $y$-component, so $u_{x}=5\text{m s}^{-1}$ and $u_{y}=0$; the acceleration gives $a_{x}=3\text{m s}^{-2}$ and $a_{y}=2\text{m s}^{-2}$.

Along $x$, with $x=84\text{m}$:

$84=5t+\dfrac{1}{2}(3)t^{2}\Rightarrow 3t^{2}+10t-168=0\Rightarrow (t-6)(3t+28)=0$

The positive root gives $t=6\text{s}$.

Velocity components at $t=6\text{s}$:

$v_{x}=5+3\times 6=23\text{m s}^{-1},v_{y}=0+2\times 6=12\text{m s}^{-1}$

$v^{2}=23^{2}+12^{2}=529+144=673\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{673}\text{m s}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 673.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: A thin metallic wire having cross sectional area of $10^{-4}\mathrm{m}^{2}$ is used to make a ring of radius $30\mathrm{cm}$. A positive charge of $2π\mathrm{C}$ is uniformly distributed over the ring, while another positive charge of 30 $\mathrm{pC}$ is kept at the centre of the ring. The tension in the ring is $______$ $\mathrm{N}$; provided that the ring does not get deformed (neglect the influence of gravity). (given, $\frac{1}{4π𝜖_{0}}=9\times 10^{9}$ SI units)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The charge per unit length of the ring is $λ=\dfrac{Q}{2πR}$. A small element subtending $dθ$ at the centre carries charge $λRdθ$, and the charge $q_{0}$ at the centre pushes it radially outward with force

$dF=\dfrac{kq_{0}(λRdθ)}{R^{2}}=\dfrac{kq_{0}λ\qquad dθ}{R}$


[IMG]

The tensions at the two ends of the element have a net inward component $2T\sin \dfrac{dθ}{2}\approx Tdθ$, which balances this force:

$Tdθ=\dfrac{kq_{0}λ\qquad dθ}{R}\Rightarrow T=\dfrac{kq_{0}λ}{R}=\dfrac{kq_{0}Q}{2πR^{2}}$

With $Q=2π\text{C}$, $q_{0}=30\times 10^{-12}\text{C}$ and $R=0.30\text{m}$:

$T=\dfrac{9\times 10^{9}\times 30\times 10^{-12}\times 2π}{2π\times (0.30)^{2}}=\dfrac{0.27}{0.09}=3\text{N}$

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift

text: In a nuclear fission process, a high mass nuclide $(A\approx 236)$ with binding energy $7.6\mathrm{MeV}/$ Nucleon dissociated into middle mass nuclides $(\mathrm{A}\approx 118)$, having binding energy of $8.6\mathrm{MeV}/\mathrm{Nucleon}$. The energy released in the process would be $______$ $\mathrm{MeV}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the energy released in a nuclear fission process, we use the difference in binding energy (BE) before and after the fission. The formula for energy released ($Q$ value) in the process is given by:
$Q=(\text{Total BE of products})-(\text{Total BE of reactants})$
In this case, the reactant is a high mass nuclide with atomic mass $A\approx 236$ and a binding energy of $7.6\mathrm{MeV}/\mathrm{nucleon}$. Each of the two middle mass nuclides formed as products has atomic mass $A\approx 118$ and a binding energy of $8.6\mathrm{MeV}/\mathrm{nucleon}$.
Therefore, we calculate the total binding energy of reactant and products as follows:
For reactant:
$\text{BE}_{\text{reactant}}=236\times 7.6\mathrm{MeV}$
For products (since there are two identical products):
$\text{BE}_{\text{products}}=2\times (118\times 8.6)\mathrm{MeV}$
Thus, the energy released ($Q$ value) is:
$Q=\text{BE}_{\text{products}}-\text{BE}_{\text{reactant}}$
$Q=2(118\times 8.6)-(236\times 7.6)$
$Q=236\times (8.6-7.6)$
$Q=236\times 1$
$Q=236\mathrm{MeV}$
This calculation demonstrates how the difference in binding energy per nucleon before and after fission leads to the release of energy, consistent with the mass-energy equivalence principle.

text:
Four particles each of mass $1\mathrm{kg}$ are placed at four corners of a square of side $2\mathrm{m}$. Moment of inertia of system about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through one of its vertex is $_____$ $\mathrm{kgm}^{2}$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{I}=\mathrm{ma}^{2}+\mathrm{ma}^{2}+\mathrm{m}(\sqrt{2}\mathrm{a})^{2} \\ =4\mathrm{ma}^{2} \\ =4\times 1\times (2)^{2}=16 \end{array}$

text: A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of $4\mathrm{cm}$. At the mean position, velocity of the particle is $10\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$. The distance of the particle from the mean position when its speed becomes $5\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}$ is $\sqrt{α}\mathrm{cm}$, where $α=$ $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{V}_{\text{at mean position}}=\mathrm{A}ω\Rightarrow 10=4ω \\ ω=\dfrac{5}{2} \\ \mathrm{V}=ω\sqrt{\mathrm{A}^{2}-\mathrm{x}^{2}} \\ 5=\dfrac{5}{2}\sqrt{4^{2}-\mathrm{x}^{2}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{x}^{2}=16-4 \\ \mathrm{x}=\sqrt{12}\mathrm{cm} \end{array}$

text:
Two long, straight wires carry equal currents in opposite directions as shown in figure. The separation between the wires is $5.0\mathrm{cm}$. The magnitude of the magnetic field at a point $\mathrm{P}$ midway between the wires is $_______$ $μ\mathrm{T}$

(Given : $μ_{0}=4π\times 10^{-7}\mathrm{TmA}^{-1}$)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{B}=\left (\dfrac{μ_{0}\mathrm{i}}{2π\mathrm{a}}\right )\times 2=\dfrac{4π\times 10^{-7}\times 10}{π\times \left (\frac{5}{2}\times 10^{-2}\right )} \\ =16\times 10^{-5}=160μ\mathrm{T} \end{array}$

text:
The charge accumulated on the capacitor connected in the following circuit is $_______$ $μ\mathrm{C}$ (Given $\mathrm{C}=150μ\mathrm{F})$


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}+\dfrac{10}{3}(1)-6(1)=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}} \\ \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}-\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}=6-\dfrac{10}{3}=\dfrac{8}{3}\mathrm{volt} \\ \mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{A}}-\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}) \\ =150\times \dfrac{8}{3}=400μ\mathrm{C} \end{array}$

text: If average depth of an ocean is $4000\mathrm{m}$ and the bulk modulus of water is $2\times 10^{9}\mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$, then fractional compression $\frac{\Delta V}{V}$ of water at the bottom of ocean is $α\times 10^{-2}$. The value of $α$ is $_______ ($Given, $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{ms}^{-2},ρ=1000\mathrm{kg}\mathrm{m}^{-3}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 27th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{B}=-\dfrac{\Delta \mathrm{P}}{\left (\frac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{V}}\right )} \\ -\left (\dfrac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{V}}\right )=\dfrac{ρ\mathrm{gh}}{\mathrm{B}}=\dfrac{1000\times 10\times 4000}{2\times 10^{9}} \\ =2\times 10^{-2}[-\mathrm{ve}\text{sign represent compression}] \end{array}$
